title: Protocol for culturing and imaging of ectodermal cells from Xenopus
protocol: Microinject DNA plasmids expressing LAMP-1-RFP or CD63-RFP into animal caps of Xenopus embryos.
Culture the injected animal cap cells to study lysosome movements in an in vivo model.
Inject xWnt8 mRNA and CD-63-RFP multivesicular body marker into animal cap cells to study Wnt signaling effects on lysosome accumulation.
Add SiR-Lysosome to culture medium to label active lysosomes containing Cathepsin D.
Increase lysosomal activation using lithium chloride (LiCl) treatment.
Dilute SiR-Lysosome from a 1 mM stock to a working concentration of 1 μM in culture medium.
Use 0.5 μL of the reagent per 500 μL of L-15 medium, which is diluted with water by 50%.
Fertilize Xenopus laevis embryos in vitro using excised testes and culture them in 0.1 × MMR solution.
Inject frog embryos with DNAs or mRNAs (for example, 20 pg per blastomere of LAMP1-RFP or CD63-RFP DNAs) at the animal pole when they are at 2–4 cell stage.
Culture the injected frog embryos until midblastula stage 8.5 before excision.
Dissect animal caps at blastula stage 8.5–9 in 1 × MMR solution.
Dissociate the cap manually by pipetting the caps 3–5 times with a glass Pasteur pipette in 1 × MMR solution.
Plate the cells in L-15 medium diluted to 50% with H2O on fibronectin-coated coverslips in a 12-well plate.
Incubate the cells for 12–18 hours between 15°C–20°C in normal atmosphere.
Wash cells with PBS three times to remove dead cells.
Fix cells for 15 min using 4% Formaldehyde diluted in PBS (4% PFA) at 20°C with limited light exposure.
Wash cells with PBS three times to remove PFA.
Apply mounting medium with DAPI onto a glass microscope slide using 10 μL per coverslip.
Place the coverslip carefully onto the mounting medium to avoid air bubbles.
Examine RFP and GFP under a Carl Zeiss Axio Observer Z1 Inverted Microscope with Apotome and Nomarski differential interference contrast (DIC) filters for DAPI, FITC, and rhodamine.
Acquire images using 63× objectives and the Zeiss Zen software.
Plate dissociated animal cap cells in a glass-bottom chamber for live-cell analysis.
Insert cell chamber for live imaging with conditions in the inverted microscope at 20°C (without CO2).
Image cells for 72 hours with an image acquisition rate of 1 frame per 30 seconds.
Incubate cells with SiR-Lysosome in 50% L-15 culture medium for 60 minutes at room temperature (500 μL per well).
Dilute TMR-Dextran 70 kDa (1 mg/mL) in 50% L-15 culture medium.
Incubate cells with the diluted TMR-Dextrin for 60 min at room temperature.
Microinject frog embryos at the 2–4 cell stage with 20 pg of DNA/cell encoding Tes-GFP or LifeAct.
Culture animal cap cells on fibronectin-coated glass-bottom chambers.
Monitor changes in cell-cell adhesion and cell migration using live-cell analyses.
Wash cells three times with PBS after incubation with growth factor or drugs.
Mount the cell chamber for live imaging on an inverted microscope.
Generate movie conditions as previously described in the culturing animal cap cells section for lysosomal studies.
Wash cells 3 times in 50% L-15 medium.
Mount a cell chamber for live imaging on an inverted microscope at room temperature.
Add GSK3 inhibitors (40 mM LiCl) or controls (40 mM NaCl or DMSO).
Start recording immediately after adding the drug treatments.
Generate a movie using the same conditions used to film before drug treatment.
Wash cells 3 times with PBS to remove dead cells.
Fix cells for 15 min in 4% PFA diluted in PBS.
Wash cells 3 times with PBS to remove PFA.
Permeabilize cells with digitonin (6.5 μg/mL) for 10 min in PBS.
Wash cells 3 times with PBS to remove detergent.
Block cells for 1 h in blocking solution containing 5% bovine serum albumin in PBS.
Incubate the samples with the primary antibody for 24 h at 4°C.
Wash cells 3 times with PBS.
Incubate with secondary antibodies for 1 hour at 20°C (0.5 mL per well).
Wash 3 times with PBS (0.5 mL per well).
Mount cells in mounting media with DAPI.
Dry slides in a dark area at 20°C for 16 hours prior to imaging.
